topic: Peptides your body makes: endothelin, the blood vessels' own squeeze signal. Endothelin-1 is a 21-amino-acid peptide made mainly by vascular endothelial cells (the inner lining), released continuously; found in 1988 by Yanagisawa, Masaki et al. at the University of Tsukuba (Nature 332:411) as one of the most potent vasoconstrictors known; long-lasting constriction of human mammary artery maintained over 2 hours in vitro, reversed by nitric oxide; balance between ET-1 and NO set partly by shear stress (Davenport et al., Pharmacol Rev 2016); NO as endothelial relaxing signal, Nobel Prize 1998 Furchgott, Ignarro, Murad (nobelprize.org); sarafotoxins from Atractaspis snake venom are structurally near to endothelins (Patocka et al., Acta Medica 2004)

cards.html:
Peptides your body makes

Your blood vessels make their own squeeze signal.

Meet endothelin

21

amino acids. Made by the thin inner lining of your blood vessels.

Found in Japan

1988

One of the strongest vessel squeezers ever found.

Slow and strong

2+ hrs

Lab tests on human arteries: one dose squeezed for over 2 hours.

The brake

Nitric oxide.

Made by the same lining. It relaxes vessels.

Plot twist

Snake venom has a lookalike.

Sarafotoxins, from burrowing asp snakes, are built almost the same.

Save this for your physiology exam.

Sources in the caption.
